headline: Dry high pressure holds through Monday; cool Bluegrass nights contrast with warmer Upstate afternoons
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Surface high pressure keeps Danville and the Bluegrass sunny and dry through Monday. Highs stay in the middle 70s, while clear skies and light wind favor chilly nights, especially in sheltered valleys.

days.label: Saturday
days.forecast: Sunny and dry after a cool start. Northeast wind remains light, generally 2–7 mph. Mostly clear skies tonight support a quick temperature drop, with the coldest readings in sheltered Bluegrass locations.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: None expected; patchy late-night valley fog cannot be ruled out
days.forecast: Sunny with light north wind. Dry air and clear skies persist Sunday night. Sheltered valleys may fall into the middle 40s, several degrees below more exposed sites.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: Brief patchy fog possible around sunrise, mainly in valleys
days.forecast: Any shallow valley fog should dissipate shortly after sunrise, followed by another sunny and dry day. Light north wind turns variable as high pressure begins to shift east. Monday night remains clear and seasonably cool.

kentucky.bottomLine: Confidence is high in a dry three-day stretch with afternoon highs in the 70s. The main uncertainty is nighttime temperature placement in sheltered valleys, especially Sunday night, plus a small window for shallow sunrise fog Monday.
kentucky.confidence: High overall; moderate on sheltered-valley lows and localized fog

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: Dry high pressure dominates Clemson and Central through Monday. Sunny afternoons reach the lower to middle 80s, while clear nights begin cool and then moderate by Monday night.

currentConditions.condition: Network observations are WeatherFlow–Tempest-fed and excluded; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Saturday
days.forecast: Sunny and dry with a light west to northwest breeze, generally 3 mph or less near Clemson. Clear skies and nearly calm wind tonight allow temperatures to fall into the lower 50s, with colder pockets near Pickens.

days.label: Sunday
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and warm with light west to southwest wind. Humidity stays comfortable for late September, and clear skies continue Sunday night.

days.label: Monday
days.forecast: Sunny with a light southwest breeze and another lower-to-middle-80s afternoon. Dry high pressure prevents meaningful convection. Monday night stays clear but turns a few degrees milder.

upstate.bottomLine: The Upstate forecast is high confidence: sunny, rain-free and warm each afternoon through Monday, with no organized hazardous weather signal.

sourceNotes: NWS point forecasts for Danville and Clemson were generated at 6:57 AM EDT. Official airport observations span 6:15–6:35 AM EDT, and Kentucky Mesonet DANV reported at 6:55 AM EDT.

The Louisville and Greenville-Spartanburg Area Forecast Discussions were issued at 6:47 AM and 6:46 AM EDT, respectively. Both support dry weather through the 72-hour period; Louisville notes a warming trend just beyond it, while Greenville-Spartanburg keeps dry high pressure dominant through at least Thursday.
The NWS active-alert API returned no active alerts for either the Danville or Clemson forecast point at the 7:01 AM EDT check. This official-alert status is separate from the independent analysis.

NOMADS inventories checked at 7:01 AM EDT showed HRRR and RAP through 10Z, complete 06Z NAM guidance through forecast hour 72, and 06Z GFS and GEFS guidance through forecast hour 72. NEXLAB showed complete 09Z RAP, 06Z NAM/NAM Nest, and 00Z ECMWF cycles; the 10Z HRRR and 06Z global ensemble panels were still ingesting but the needed guidance was independently available and verified.

College of DuPage NEXLAB panels were checked directly. The 10:51 AM UTC visible satellite showed clear skies across both forecast regions, and the 10:55 AM UTC Southeast radar mosaic showed no organized echoes over either region. NAM Nest simulated reflectivity remained quiet locally through Monday afternoon.

Clemson Weather Network identifies its observations as WeatherFlow–Tempest data. Those observations were excluded, and official KCEU and KLQK observations were used for Upstate analysis and verification.
Radar and satellite links remain external and live; the existing Google Sites radar section is not modified by this candidate.
